fields.features_heading: The Seats in Each Section, and Who Holds Them
fields.features_subheading: A class registration form signs a student up for one class and section. This one counts the open seats while they choose.
fields.feature_1:
Each section keeps its own seat limit

Every section of a class carries its own meeting time and its own seat limit. Once the last seat is taken, the form stops offering that section and points to the next open one.
fields.feature_2:
Guardian details only for minors

When the birth date puts a student under 18, the form asks for a parent or guardian's phone number and an emergency contact. Adult students skip that page of the form entirely.
fields.feature_3:
One question per screen on a phone

A parent registering from a phone sees one question per screen. The class list shows as large choices to tap instead of a dense grid that needs pinching and zooming to read.
fields.feature_4:
Confirmation with the room and start date

Each registrant gets an email naming the section they joined and the room it meets in. A reminder email follows before the first session, on whatever schedule you set.
fields.feature_5:
A roster per section, in your database

Every sign-up is a row in a database you own, with no cap on responses. The roster for any section is a filtered view of those rows, not a spreadsheet someone retypes.
fields.feature_6:
The code goes to GitHub on paid plans

On paid plans, export the full code of the form and its database to your GitHub repository, where a developer of your own can read every line of it and change what you need.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Class Providers Run Their Sign-Ups
fields.tab_content_1:
In Spanish or English, one table for all 112 sign-ups

Tarrow Park Recreation Center's spring form asks for English or Spanish on the first screen. Inocencia Barragan picks Spanish, signs her daughter up for Saturday Ceramics for Kids, and gets her confirmation email in Spanish. Staff read all 112 spring registrations in one English table, 29 of the 112 marked Spanish.
fields.tab_content_2:
After a Tuesday clash, Tap I moves to Thursday

Brassmoor Dance Studio lets a new student pick up to 3 weekly classes. Tamsin Ogundipe picks Jazz II, a 60-minute class on Tuesday at 5:00 PM, then Tap I on Tuesday at 5:30 PM. The form shows that Tap I overlaps Jazz II and offers the Tap I section on Thursday at 5:30 PM, which she takes.
fields.tab_content_3:
Current or expired, the CPR card date decides the seat

Halvering County Fire Training Center wants a current CPR card from everyone in its April 14 pump operations class, so the form asks for the card's expiration date and a photo. Oriel Lindqvist enters a card that expired March 30. Her seat is held, and coordinator Desmond Achterberg gets an email asking him to review it.
fields.tab_content_4:
Six by January 10, or Tuesday pottery goes to Thursday

Wexcombe Community Education runs a Beginning Pottery section only when 6 adults register by January 10. On January 11, the Tuesday section has 4 and the Thursday section has 9. The app tells the Tuesday group by email that their section will not run and offers Thursday. Barnaby Quist moves over from that email.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Class Registration Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up a class registration form around your sections and their seat limits, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put age on the first screen
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every class you run this term, then each section under it with its day, start time, length, room, and seat limit. Treat each section as its own row, since a seat limit or a minimum applies to one section, not to the whole class.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for the participant's name and birth date before anything else. Age decides which classes a child can see, and a 6-year-old never scrolls past adult pottery. It also decides which contact questions come next.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Note the checks a class needs before a seat counts. One class wants a current prerequisite card, another a minimum number of sign-ups by a cutoff date. Each check becomes one line of your prompt.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put the classes and those checks into a prompt. Emergent builds the form, the database table behind it, and a roster view for each section. Read the first draft as a parent would, then ask for changes in plain words.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Register twice before you share it
fields.howto_step_5_des: Register as a parent with two children, then as an adult taking an evening class. Pick a full section and two classes in one time slot, and confirm the form catches both and the confirmation email names the right room.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Set the emails and when they send
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide what each email says and when it goes out. The confirmation sends right after a sign-up, a reminder 2 days before the first session, and a notice whenever a section will not run. Name the class and its room in each one.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Share one link for the whole term
fields.howto_step_7_des: Share one link on your schedule page and at the front desk. Sign-ups land in the database as they arrive, and each section's roster is ready for its instructor on the first day of class.

faq_plan.q: What is a class registration form?
faq_plan.a: A class registration form is the form a student, or a parent for a child, fills in to take a seat in a specific class and section. It records who is taking the class and which section they chose, plus any contact or prerequisite details needed before the first session.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a class registration form?
faq_plan.a: Describe your classes and their seat limits in a prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. It builds the form and saves every sign-up to a database you own, and you change any rule later by asking in plain words. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What should a class registration form template include?
faq_plan.a: A class registration form template should include the student's full name and birth date, plus the class and section they want. Add contact details, with a guardian and an emergency contact for anyone under 18. Add prerequisite or skill-level questions only to the classes that need them. The same sections apply if you also keep a class registration form PDF at the front desk.

faq_plan.q: How should a class registration form handle a class that runs for several weeks?
faq_plan.a: Register once for the whole run, not week by week. List the section with the dates of its first and last sessions and the day it meets. One sign-up then holds the seat for every session. If the program runs for whole days over the summer and families pick weeks, a summer camp registration form fits better.

faq_plan.q: Can a class registration form keep a waitlist for a full section?
faq_plan.a: Yes. When a section reaches its seat limit, the form offers a waitlist spot instead, and waitlisted students are saved in the order they joined. When someone drops, the app emails the first person on the list a link to claim the seat within a time you set, such as 48 hours. Emergent builds the waitlist and its emails from the same prompt as the form.

faq_plan.q: Should a class registration form take payment at sign-up?
faq_plan.a: Take payment at sign-up when you want a seat to count only once it is paid. If an employer or a school pays later, collect the billing contact instead and mark the row unpaid. The app connects to your payment tool through its API, and each payment is recorded on the registrant's row.

faq_plan.q: Can one class registration form cover several classes at once?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Show the class list with the sections under each class, let the student pick as many as you allow, and save one row per class picked so every section's roster stays accurate. For a multi-day event with sessions and badges, a conference registration form is the better fit.

faq_plan.q: How do I let students switch sections after they submit a class registration form?
faq_plan.a: Put a link to their own registration in the confirmation email. From it, a student picks a section with open seats; the app frees the old seat and emails both instructors. Set a cutoff, such as the day before the first session, after which changes go through staff. Emergent adds that change link when you ask for it in the prompt.

faq_plan.q: Can a class registration form work in more than one language?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Write each question once per language and save every answer to the same field, and one table holds all sign-ups whatever language they came in. Have a fluent speaker check each translation before launch, and keep class names identical across versions to match rosters. Emergent builds both versions from one prompt and saves them to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What age details should a class registration form for kids collect?
faq_plan.a: Collect the birth date, not the age. A child who is 7 at sign-up may turn 8 before the class starts, and the birth date lets the form check eligibility against the first day of class. For ongoing childcare rather than a class with a set term, a daycare registration form collects the schedule and pickup details that care needs.
